title: Anchor Decay — Experiment Notebook
content:
Quick summary:
- Investigate how an explicit directive (the "anchor") in the system+prompt or first few examples degrades as more context/tokens are added downstream (user messages, long few-shot exemplars, generated assistant tokens).
- Practical goal: find robust micro-patterns to keep anchor effect stable across long-turn dialogues without adding too many tokens.

Background notes (definition):
- Anchor = a short, strong constraint or behavior spec (tone / disambiguation / identity / system rule) placed early in context.
- Anchor decay = the observed weakening of the model following the anchor when later context contradicts or simply pushes token distance.

Experiment matrix (rough):
- Anchor types: explicit-system-sentence / footnote-in-exemplar / last-example-summarizer
- Context lengths: 0 (control), +200 tokens, +1000 tokens, +3000 tokens
- Models: rdlw-quantized-13b-v1, open-7b-optimized (use Redwood dev tokens)
- Metrics: anchor-fidelity (binary pass/fail on 5 seed tests), soft-violation-score (0..1 per response), token-position-of-first-violation

Few-shot sets used (minimal, intentionally compact):
- Template A (3-shot, anchored):
  SYSTEM: You are a concise, professional assistant.
  EX1: Q: Convert to bullet points. A: [bulleted answer]
  EX2: Q: Summarize with a one-line takeaway. A: [one-liner]
  EX3: Q: Translate to plain language. A: [plain answer]
  USER: Long user query (varied) -> expected: concise/professional response

- Template B (3-shot, anchored but examples contradictory):
  SYSTEM: You are a concise, professional assistant.
  EX1..EX3: examples intentionally verbose (to test overwrite)
  USER: same test queries -> expected failures highlight decay

Observed failure modes (notes from runs on 2026-02-05):
- Slow drift: model remains anchored for ~3 answers then drifts into verbosity.
- Late contradiction: when user includes an example that conflicts with anchor, model follows the last user example despite anchor at top.
- Token-distance leakage: anchors that are >1200 tokens away tend to be ignored in ~70% of trials for rdlw-quantized-13b-v1.
- Example contamination: If one exemplar uses different domain-specific jargon, model starts to adopt jargon and loses anchor tone.

Representative failing transcript (abbreviated):
  [SYSTEM] You are concise and professional.
  EX1..EX3 (compact)
  USER: Extremely long multi-paragraph context (~900 tokens) that includes a sample answer in a casual tone.
  ASSISTANT: starts concise -> at ~3rd paragraph of reply, reverts to casual, story-like phrasing.
  Notes: first violation at token ~480 of response, soft-violation-score 0.62

Hypotheses (quick):
- Model places decaying attention weight on early tokens as context grows.
- Kernel scheduling/kv-cache truncation threshold in serving runtime might be affecting effective attention window (esp. quantized variants).
- Few-shot exemplars close to user prompt have outsized influence because of recency bias; anchor needs repeated reinforcement or embedding-level caching.

Mitigations to test (priority order):
1) Anchor repetition: sprinkle a 6-8 token anchor phrase every ~700 tokens in the prompt (experiment: static vs generated repetition).
2) Anchor summarizer: after each long user chunk, prepend a 12-token reminder auto-generated by a small summarizer model and fed into the next request.
3) Position-weighted examples: place the most important exemplar last to leverage recency instead of earliest-system-only anchors.
4) Soft constraints via prefixed instruction tokens (try tokenized anchors that survive quantization).

Quick prompts to reproduce locally (copy/paste):
- CONTROL (short):
  system: "You are concise and professional. Answer in 3 bullet points."
  user: "Explain X in simple terms."

- LONG CONTEXT (repro):
  system: "You are concise and professional. Answer in 3 bullet points."
  user: "[insert ~1000 tokens of background that include a contradictory example answer]"
  expected: concise (fail occurs if >1 sentence per bullet or narrative appears)

Small experiment results (sanity log):
- 2026-02-07: rdlw-13b, control -> pass 9/10
- 2026-02-07: rdlw-13b, +1000 tokens -> pass 3/10 (anchor repetition improved to 7/10)
- 2026-02-10: open-7b-optimized, +1000 tokens -> pass 2/10 (anchor summarizer improved to 6/10)

Notes-to-self:
- Need to instrument token-level attention weights if possible (trace hooks in serving-runtime) to confirm decay shape.
- Check KV cache truncation policy and any heuristics that might drop early tokens for long conversations (talk to infra: @Noah).
- Try embedding-based anchor: compute anchor embedding and include nearest neighbor hints before each request (cheap Llama-2 microservice?).

Open questions:
- Is this mostly a modeling artifact or an inference/runtime artifact? (how to tease apart?)
- What is the unit-cost tradeoff if we repeat anchors every 500 tokens? Is that cheaper than running a small summarizer model each turn?

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run ablation with anchor repetition vs summarizer vs last-example recency for 3 models (rdlw-13b, rdlw-7b, open-7b-optimized) (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Add tracing hooks into dev serving-runtime to capture token position of first soft-violation (owner: Noah)
- [ ] Create a 50-query prompt-bench suite specifically designed to detect anchor decay (link to PR #88) (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Post findings to confluence + short sync with SRE (owner: Maya)

Side ideas (for later):
- Adaptive anchor: model-internal sentinel that outputs a "compliance-check" token strip at every 8th turn (toy idea).
- Training-side: small RL fine-tune to preserve anchor compliance across long contexts (expensive but might generalize).

Misc links and quick refs:
- Linear ticket for bench tracking: RED-4123
- Draft PR with bench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-bench/pull/88
- Slack: thread G6V3xk in #prompt-lab has sample transcripts

Random scratch snippets:
- "Anchor repeat" phrase attempt: "NOTE: keep answers concise (<=3 bullets)" - inserted at top + every 600 tokens -> seems to help.
- Quick metric idea: measure lexical entropy change pre/post violation window (low effort, use existing bench infra).

End of notebook (for now).
- Maya
